title: Resilient dependency guard and rollback-safe routing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a graduated dependency-guarding mechanism that combines multi-dimensional trip scoring (latency, error rate, queue depth, and token-per-second consumption) with rollback-safe routing policies. Goal: detect degradation early for a dependency (model / external service / tenant) and route requests to safe fallbacks without breaking end-user SLOs or data isolation requirements. This ticket covers the design, implementation, integration tests, and a canary rollout configuration for the runtime and the routing layer.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes per-dependency health score (0-100) computed from latency p95, error-rate, and inflight queue size
Routing service consumes health score and applies policy to route to: primary, degraded model (quantized or lower-context variant), cached prefix, or secondary region
Fallbacks must preserve tenant isolation and respect model version pinning

Automated integration tests simulate slowdowns and verify that 99% of requests that hit fallbacks still meet the degraded SLOs defined in doc: minimum availability 99.5% and 95th latency target for degraded path <= 600ms
Playbook and rollback procedure documented; canary rollout enabled with 1% traffic for first 24h, automatic rollback on error-rate spike > 1.5x baseline
tasks: Design: multi-dimensional trip score algorithm and weight tuning (PM + SRE)
Runtime: add metric exporter for per-dependency scores and short-term spike window
Routing: implement score consumer and routing policy engine with fallback chain support
Fallbacks: integrate cached-prefix store + quantized model variants + regional warm-standby routing
Testing: unit tests for scoring, integration tests for end-to-end degraded routing
Observability: dashboard with time-series of score components, decision logs, and canary telemetry
Operational: author playbook, runbook, and rollback procedures; SLO smoke tests
